summary: RAG anti-modal contrast topology on champion LoRA v2a_e1
hypothesis: Applying the ragAntiModalContrast in-context topology (from exp027) to the champion LoRA adapter v2a_e1 should beat the current best, because combining a proven retrieval-contrast prompt structure with the best fine-tuned weights might push past the coverage wall the adapter alone cannot clear.
technique: A RAG-augmented in-context pipeline using the anti-modal contrast topology (originally from exp027) is crossed onto the champion LoRA adapter v2a_e1, run greedy/deterministic — part of an all-inference × best-LoRA matrix sweep.
result: Scored 0.470 on the full-30 greedy eval (6 wins / 4 ties / 20 losses vs Sonnet), with rubric atom=4, spec=4, cover=3, nat=4, nonRed=3; initially logged as a new best (kept=true). However, re-judging the identical deterministic output (exp079) scored 0.402 — a 0.068 swing attributable purely to stochastic judge noise — putting the mean at ~0.436, squarely within the noise band around champion exp056 (0.440). The 0.470 was the top of the judge-noise band; the anti-modal contrast topology on the adapter ties the champion within noise and does not beat it, and the coverage wall (cover=3) holds.
